claim.why_it_matters: The Latin row of the C.2.1 repertoire table is cut at the printed line wrap: the table cell ends with the dangling range start '0250-' and the rest of the row ('02A8, 1E00-1E9B, 1EA0-1EF9, 207F') sits in a separate paragraph outside the table. A reader of the table sees an unterminated range and loses the Latin ranges 0250-02A8, 1E00-1E9B, 1EA0-1EF9 and 207F from the Latin row.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (p.698 of ISO/IEC 1989:2002, PDF page 720) shows the Latin row wrapping after '0250-' onto a second line '02A8, 1E00-1E9B, 1EA0-1EF9, 207F'. page-720.md line 36 ends the table cell with '0250-' and line 38 carries '02A8, 1E00-1E9B, 1EA0-1EF9, 207F' immediately after, before the Greek row (which is itself rendered as a plain paragraph). Every code value is present, in the printed order, and nothing comes between the two halves; the only difference is that the printed line wrap broke the markdown table structure. That is a line-wrap/table-formatting artifact, not a content discrepancy: no range is lost or changed and no other row's values intervene, so a reader reflowing the wrap gets the exact printed list.
